name: V01 cellAtLine: the search starts at the second cell
why: the first cell can never be found; killed by the named rows and every enumerated document whose only cell is the first (cellAt on every line against findCellAtPosition)

name: V02 cellAtLine: the search stops before the last cell
why: the last cell can never be found; killed by the same differential (a one-cell document) and by the clock rows' read-back of the last cell

name: V03 cellAtLine: nothing found starts at the first cell
why: a line above the first cell (prose, line 0, -1) answers the first cell, and a document with no cell reads cells[0] of an empty array (a TypeError); killed by the no-cell named row and the differential

name: V04 cellAtLine: a cell starts strictly above its first line
why: the opening fence line is not in its cell (findCellAtPosition is inclusive of it); killed by the cellAt row on a fence line and by every enumerated document

name: V05 cellAtLine: the cell found is the one before
why: the answer is always the previous cell (or none for the first); killed by the cellAt rows and the differential

name: V06 cellAtLine: the middle is not an integer
why: an odd sum gives a half index, cells[1.5] is undefined and reading its startLine throws; killed by any document with two or more cells and a lookup that probes an odd sum (E2, the seeded documents, the clock rows)

name: V07 cellAtLine: the first cell is never answered
from: return found >= 0 && line <= cells[found].endLine ? cells[found] : null;
to: return found > 0 && line <= cells[found].endLine ? cells[found] : null;
why: index 0 is a cell that was found; killed like V01

name: V08 cellAtLine: the closing fence line is outside the cell
from: return found >= 0 && line <= cells[found].endLine ? cells[found] : null;
to: return found >= 0 && line < cells[found].endLine ? cells[found] : null;
why: findCellAtPosition is inclusive of the closing fence (R2); killed by the cellAt rows and every enumerated document with a cell

name: V09 cellAtLine: a line past the cell still answers it
from: return found >= 0 && line <= cells[found].endLine ? cells[found] : null;
why: prose under a cell answers the cell; killed by the cellAt row (line 4 of the five-line text) and the differential

name: V10 cellAtLine: the end line is compared with the start line
from: return found >= 0 && line <= cells[found].endLine ? cells[found] : null;
to: return found >= 0 && line <= cells[found].startLine ? cells[found] : null;
why: only the fence line answers; killed by the body-line lookups of the named rows and the differential
